title: Model batch
description: An atomic batch of element creates, updates and deletes, database schema operations, materialize operations, process operations, tag operations and the names-to-ids refactor, from the editor, a refactoring or an AI proposal.

id.description: The element: an id, a qualified name (@kind:path) or a placeholder ($name). A create's id must be an id; an update's or delete's must not be a placeholder.

as.description: Create and update: a placeholder that names the operation's element for the whole batch.

resolution.description: What a delete does with references to the element: refuse (the default) while anything references it, remove-references to clear optional references, or delete-dependents to also remove or delete what cannot exist without it (delete only).

element.description: The element document. Its references may be qualified names or placeholders, and an object whose schema requires an id may carry as; the engine mints every missing id below the root.

value.description: The translated text, a sidecar reference, or null to remove the translation.

database.description: The database: an id, a qualified name or a placeholder (materialize-tables, materialize-entities, materialize-attributes, materialize-columns).

entities.description: The entities, each an id, a qualified name or a placeholder, that get a designed table and a binding (materialize-tables), or that get an attribute per column of the source of their binding to the database (materialize-attributes), or a column of their table per attribute their binding leaves unmapped (materialize-columns).

tables.description: The designed or imported tables and the views, each an id, a qualified name or a placeholder, that get an entity and a binding (materialize-entities).

package.description: The package the new entities go to (materialize-entities); the domain whose tag vocabulary it is (retag, tags-to-property; absent for the global one). An id, a qualified name or a placeholder.

columns.description: The columns of the source, as keys or physical names, that get an attribute mapped to them (materialize-attributes, one entity only); absent means every column nothing in the binding names.

attributes.description: The binding field references (attribute ids, attributeId.memberId for a value object member, to-one end ids) that get a column of the entity's table mapped to them (materialize-columns, one entity only); absent means every attribute the binding leaves unmapped. An item that starts with @ or $ names one attribute or end; the composite attributeId.memberId stays ids.

elementIds.description: The elements names-to-ids and tags-to-property act on, each an id, a qualified name or a placeholder; absent means every element they apply to (names-to-ids: every document with x-ref sites; tags-to-property: every holder the vocabulary governs, and the moved tags' declarations leave the vocabulary).

tags.description: The tag keys to remove, or the one to rename (retag).

prefix.description: The prefix of the tags that move into the property name (tags-to-property): each tag that starts with it and leaves a non-empty suffix.

expectedHashes.description: Materialize, retag, tags-to-property and names-to-ids: the hash the caller read of each element it expects the operation to change or delete (the preview's updates and deletes). Given, an element that changed since, or that the operation changes but the map does not name, is a conflict and nothing is written, so an undo built from what the caller read never puts back a stale version. A key may be a qualified name, never a placeholder.

schema.description: The database schema: an id, a qualified name or a placeholder (rename-schema, remove-schema, set-default-schema; optional for add-schema; for materialize-tables, the schema the tables go to, else each projected table's own).

name.description: The schema name (add-schema, rename-schema); the new key of the one tag (retag; absent removes the tags); the custom property the tags move to (tags-to-property).

target.description: The schema that the tables, views, sequences, convention entries and mappings of the removed schema move to (remove-schema); the process the entity follows, or absent to clear the lifecycle (set-lifecycle); the child state that becomes the initial one (set-initial). An id, a qualified name or a placeholder.

default.description: The schema that becomes the default when the removed schema is the default (remove-schema): an id, a qualified name or a placeholder.

placeholder.description: A name a batch declares with as and uses anywhere in the batch.

qualifiedName.description: An element or sub-element by kind and stored name: @kind:path, its segments separated by dots, a segment with a dot, quote or white space written in double quotes.

idOrName.description: An id, a qualified name or a placeholder.
